expectations.text: Final report includes per-interface smoke-test results with URL and status alongside the per-item checklist table.
expectations.evidence: Line 78 has the per-item table (V1/A/B/S, Source/Command/Result/Smoke test/Evidence). Lines 87-97 have the per-interface smoke table with URL and result, including before- and after-fix statuses and 'Not reported' rows.

expectations.text: Clearly labels the trace and successful outcomes as simulated, without claiming an actual upgrade or actual command execution.
expectations.evidence: Line 3 has a disclaimer and [SIM] tags throughout, and line 76 says 'all outcomes are simulated; nothing was actually run'. But the final report's headline (line 70) states, without qualification, 'I upgraded Spring Boot 3.2.5 → **3.5.12**'. Line 74 says 'Manual fix: raised the springdoc-openapi version property', and line 106 says 'you're on the latest 3.x'. These read as claims that an actual upgrade and edit happened, which contradicts 'did not change any files'. Graded strictly, this fails.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminate smoke-test derivation and the api-docs failure well, but both runs satisfy nearly all of them, so they do not distinguish the skills. Consider adding an assertion for separate recipe-vs-agent change attribution in the final report and for not marking the stage ready while mvn clean install is unevidenced (both runs handled that).
